summary: All voucher attachment endpoints (invoices, expenses, income) verified end-to-end against the public preview backend. 9/9 pytest cases passed: single & multi-file uploads, GET persistence, deletion via ?path=, 10 MB size cap enforcement, and 404 on invalid ids for both POST and DELETE. Attachment records include the expected keys {path, name, size, content_type, uploaded_at, uploaded_by}. No backend fixes required.
critical_code_review_comments: Attachment upload path uses `run_in_threadpool(put_object, ...)` which is good; storage layer not part of this test scope but path is returned in the response so DELETE by exact path works.
Duplicate-invoice guard rail (same party+date+type) is still honored — test avoided it by using a fresh /customers/quick party per run.

10 MB cap is checked after reading the entire body into memory (`await file.read()`); for very large uploads this could OOM the worker. Consider streaming/size guard on Content-Length header before reading. Not blocking.
seed_data_creation: Each run creates one fresh customer via /api/customers/quick (random mobile + name prefixed TEST_AttachParty_), one sale invoice for today, one expense (Office/1500/cash), and one income (Consulting/2500/cash). Attachments uploaded during tests get removed via the DELETE endpoint under test, though the underlying storage objects and voucher rows remain (acceptable — they are prefixed TEST_ where applicable).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Voucher attachments (POST/DELETE + 10 MB cap + 404s) are green. Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_voucher_attachments.py can be reused; override BASE_URL via TEST_BASE_URL env var if needed. Not covered here (already covered in earlier iterations): auth, base invoice/expense/income CRUD beyond attachments, and the storage backend (`put_object`) itself.
